                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man presents to clinic complaining of increasing difficulty climbing stairs and standing up from sitting in his chair. On exam you perceive that his strength to be 5/5 distally, but only 3/5 in proximal muscle groups bilaterally. There is a distinctive rash on his upper eyelids and around his eyes. Examination of the fingers is most likely to reveal which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Dactylitis
opb. Enlargement of the PIP
opc. Ulnar deviation of the fingers
opd. Nail pitting with oil spots
ope. Violaceous papules over the MCP, PIP, and DIP

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's proximal muscle weakness and distinctive rash on the upper eyelids and around the eyes are indicative of dermatomyositis. Examination of the fingers is most likely to reveal violaceous papules over the MCP, PIP, and DIP, supporting the diagnosis of dermatomyositis.
